name: Non-profit & fundraising
tagline: Money raised, donors, average and recurring gifts, campaign cost, grants awarded and volunteer hours for charities and NGOs
description: Donation and gift exports from fundraising CRMs and giving platforms (Salesforce Nonprofit Success Pack, Blackbaud Raiser's Edge NXT and eTapestry, Bloomerang, Little Green Light, CiviCRM, Donorbox, Givebutter, Classy, JustGiving; in India Give.do, Ketto, Milaap and Razorpay or Instamojo donation pages with 80G receipts), donor lists with lifetime totals, grant registers in the 360Giving standard or from grants systems such as Fluxx and Submittable, CSR grant trackers, and volunteer hours logs (Volunteers for Salesforce, Better Impact, VolunteerHub).

fields.label: Donation / gift ID
fields.description: Identifies each donation; repeats when a gift is split across funds or soft credits.

fields.label: Donor
fields.description: The giving person or organisation: an ID, a constituent number or an email.

fields.label: Fund / programme
fields.description: Where the money goes: the fund, designation or programme a gift, grant or volunteer shift is for.

fields.label: Status
fields.description: The state of a gift, grant or volunteer shift: received or paid, pending or pledged, declined or failed, refunded.

fields.label: Acknowledgement status
fields.description: Whether the donor has been thanked or sent a receipt for the gift.

subDomains.name: Donations & gifts
subDomains.description: One row per donation or gift (or per payment of a recurring gift) with date, amount, donor, campaign, fund and payment details.

subDomains.name: Donor list
subDomains.description: One row per donor (constituent or supporter) with first and last gift dates, lifetime giving, number of gifts and status.

subDomains.name: Grants
subDomains.description: One row per grant made or applied for, as in a 360Giving file or a grants-management export, with the award date, amounts, recipient, funder and programme.

subDomains.name: Volunteer hours
subDomains.description: One row per volunteer shift or hours entry, with the volunteer, date, hours and role.

kpis.name: Total raised
kpis.definition: Money received from donations in the period, leaving out failed, refunded and still-pending (pledged) gifts.
kpis.formula: Σ donation amount, excluding declined, refunded and pending gifts

variants.label: Sum of amount
variants.caveat: No status column, so every row counts, including any failed, refunded or pledged gifts.

pitfalls: Pledges are promises: they are left out until paid, so a pledge drive shows up only as the payments arrive.
Gift Aid or matched funds added on top of a gift count only when they are rows of their own.

kpis.name: Donations
kpis.definition: Number of donations received in the period.
kpis.formula: Count of distinct gift IDs, excluding declined, refunded and pending gifts

variants.label: Distinct gift IDs
variants.caveat: No status column, so failed, refunded and pledged gifts count too.

variants.label: Rows, gifts received
variants.caveat: No gift ID, so each row is one gift.

variants.label: Row count
variants.caveat: No gift ID or status: every row counts as one gift.

kpis.name: Donors
kpis.definition: Distinct donors who gave in the period (or listed, in a donor list).
kpis.formula: Count of distinct donors with a gift received

variants.label: Distinct donor names, gifts received
variants.caveat: No donor ID, so donors are counted by name: namesakes merge and spelling variants split.

variants.label: Distinct donor names
variants.caveat: No donor ID, so donors are counted by name: namesakes merge and spelling variants split.

pitfalls: Anonymous gifts are often recorded under one placeholder donor, which counts once.

kpis.name: Average gift
kpis.definition: Average amount of one donation.
kpis.formula: Total raised ÷ donations

variants.label: Lifetime giving ÷ number of gifts
variants.caveat: From the donor list: lifetime giving ÷ number of gifts, over donors with both.

pitfalls: A few large gifts pull the average up; read the median gift beside it.

kpis.name: Recurring giving share
kpis.definition: Share of money raised that came from recurring (monthly or other regular) gifts.
kpis.formula: Raised from recurring gifts ÷ raised from gifts with a recurring flag or frequency

variants.label: Recurring frequency
variants.caveat: Uses the gift frequency: monthly, quarterly, annual and other repeating gifts count as recurring.

kpis.name: New donors
kpis.definition: Donors whose first gift falls in the period.
kpis.formula: Donors with first donation date ≥ period start

variants.label: First gift in period, by name
variants.caveat: No donor ID, so donors are matched by name.

pitfalls: Donors whose first gift predates this file look new; the longer the history, the more accurate this is.

kpis.name: Lifetime giving
kpis.definition: Everything the donors listed have given, as totalled by the CRM.
kpis.formula: Σ lifetime giving
pitfalls: CRMs differ on what a lifetime total includes (hard credits only, or soft credits and matched gifts too); check before comparing with the accounts.

kpis.name: Average lifetime giving per donor
kpis.definition: Average amount each listed donor has given over their lifetime.
kpis.formula: Σ lifetime giving ÷ donors with a lifetime total

variants.label: Lifetime giving ÷ donor names
variants.caveat: No donor ID, so donors are counted by name.

kpis.name: Lapsed donor share
kpis.definition: Share of donors whose status marks them as lapsed (no recent gift).
kpis.formula: Lapsed donors ÷ donors with a status

variants.label: Lapsed donor IDs ÷ donors with a status
Lapsed rows ÷ rows with a status
variants.caveat: No donor ID, so each row is one donor.

pitfalls: Each CRM defines lapsed in its own way (often no gift in the last 12 or 13 months); compare only within one system.

kpis.name: Amount awarded
kpis.definition: Value of grants awarded in the period.
kpis.formula: Σ amount awarded, excluding declined and pending applications

variants.label: Sum of amount awarded, grants not declined or pending
Sum of amount awarded
variants.caveat: No status column, so every row's awarded amount counts.

pitfalls: Awards are commitments, often paid over several years: never add awards and payments together.

kpis.name: Grants awarded
kpis.definition: Number of grants awarded in the period.
kpis.formula: Count of distinct grant IDs with an awarded status (or an awarded amount)

variants.label: Distinct grant IDs with an awarded amount
variants.caveat: No status column, so grants with an awarded amount count.

variants.label: Distinct grant IDs
variants.caveat: No status or awarded amount: every grant in the file counts as awarded.

variants.label: Rows with an awarded status
variants.caveat: No grant ID, so each row is one grant.

variants.label: Rows with an awarded amount
variants.caveat: No grant ID or status, so each row with an awarded amount is one grant.

kpis.name: Average grant size
kpis.definition: Average value of one grant awarded.
kpis.formula: Amount awarded ÷ grants awarded
pitfalls: A few large multi-year grants pull the average up; read the median grant beside it.

kpis.name: Grantees
kpis.definition: Distinct organisations awarded a grant in the period.
kpis.formula: Count of distinct recipients with an awarded grant

variants.label: Distinct recipients with an awarded amount
variants.caveat: No status column, so recipients with an awarded amount count.

variants.label: Distinct recipients
variants.caveat: No status or awarded amount: every recipient in the file counts.

pitfalls: Recipient names are spelt in several ways across years; use the charity or company number where the file has one.

kpis.name: Application success rate
kpis.definition: Share of decided grant applications that were funded.
kpis.formula: Awarded applications ÷ applications with a decision (pending excluded)

variants.label: Awarded ÷ decided rows
variants.caveat: No grant ID, so each row is one application.

pitfalls: A file of awarded grants only (such as a 360Giving publication) has no declined applications, so the rate reads 100%.

kpis.name: Share of ask awarded
kpis.definition: On funded grants, how much of the amount requested was awarded.
kpis.formula: Σ amount awarded ÷ Σ amount requested, on grants with both and an award above zero

kpis.name: Volunteer hours
kpis.definition: Hours given by volunteers in the period, on shifts that took place.
kpis.formula: Σ volunteer hours, excluding cancelled, no-show and upcoming shifts

variants.label: Sum of hours
variants.caveat: No status column, so every row's hours count, including any planned or cancelled shifts.

kpis.name: Active volunteers
kpis.definition: Distinct volunteers who gave time in the period.
kpis.formula: Count of distinct volunteers with hours above zero on shifts worked

variants.label: Distinct volunteers with hours, shifts worked
Distinct volunteers with hours
variants.caveat: No status column, so anyone with hours recorded counts.

variants.label: Distinct volunteers
variants.caveat: No hours column, so everyone listed counts.

kpis.name: Hours per volunteer
kpis.definition: Average hours each active volunteer gave in the period.
kpis.formula: Volunteer hours ÷ active volunteers
pitfalls: A few very committed volunteers raise the average; most volunteers usually give much less.

kpis.name: Shifts worked
kpis.definition: Volunteer shifts or hours entries that took place in the period.
kpis.formula: Rows not cancelled, no-show or upcoming

variants.label: Rows with hours
variants.caveat: No status column, so rows with hours count as shifts worked.

variants.label: Row count
variants.caveat: No status or hours column: every row counts as a shift.

kpis.name: Volunteer no-show rate
kpis.definition: Share of past volunteer shifts that were cancelled or not attended.
kpis.formula: Cancelled or no-show shifts ÷ shifts with a status (upcoming excluded)

variants.label: Cancelled or no-show ÷ shifts with a status

kpis.name: Repeat donor share
kpis.definition: Share of donors who gave two or more times.
kpis.formula: Donors with ≥ 2 gifts ÷ donors

variants.label: Donors with 2+ gifts received ÷ donors
variants.caveat: Counted from the gifts in this file: each row received is one gift.

variants.label: Donors with 2+ rows ÷ donors
variants.caveat: No status or gift count, so every row is a gift, including failed or pledged ones.

pitfalls: Grows with the length of the period: compare equal periods.
A gift split across funds or soft credits appears on several rows and can make a one-time donor look like a repeat donor.

kpis.name: Gifts per donor
kpis.definition: Average number of gifts each donor made.
kpis.formula: Donations ÷ donors

variants.label: Donations ÷ donors
variants.caveat: Counted from the gifts in this file.

kpis.name: Median gift
kpis.definition: The middle gift amount: half of gifts were smaller and half larger.
kpis.formula: Median donation amount, gifts received

variants.label: Median amount
variants.caveat: No status column, so failed, refunded and pledged gifts count too.

kpis.name: Processing fee rate
kpis.definition: Fees taken by the payment processor or giving platform as a share of the amount given.
kpis.formula: Σ fees ÷ Σ donation amount, on gifts with both
pitfalls: When donors choose to cover the fee, it is added on top of the gift; check whether your platform's amount includes it.

kpis.name: Net raised after fees
kpis.definition: Money received from donations after processing and platform fees.
kpis.formula: Σ donation amount − Σ fees, gifts received

variants.label: Amount − fees
variants.caveat: No status column, so every row counts.

pitfalls: Some platforms export the amount after fees already; check one payout before subtracting fees again.

kpis.name: Gift Aid / tax-deductible share
kpis.definition: Share of money raised from gifts eligible for tax relief (Gift Aid in the UK, 80G in India, tax-deductible receipts elsewhere).
kpis.formula: Raised from eligible gifts ÷ raised from gifts with the flag recorded

kpis.name: Cost to raise a dollar
kpis.definition: Fundraising cost spent for each unit of money raised (0.20 means 20 cents to raise a dollar).
kpis.formula: Σ fundraising cost ÷ total raised, on rows with both

benchmark.note: The BBB Wise Giving Alliance standards ask charities to spend no more than 35% of related contributions on fundraising; about 0.20 is widely cited as a typical overall cost to raise a dollar. Acquisition appeals cost far more than renewals.

pitfalls: A campaign's cost repeated on every gift row is added once per row; use a campaign-level table (one row per campaign) for this measure.

kpis.name: Fundraising goal attainment
kpis.definition: Money raised as a share of the fundraising goal.
kpis.formula: Total raised ÷ Σ campaign goal, on rows with both
pitfalls: A goal repeated on every gift row is added once per row; use a campaign-level table (one row per campaign) for this measure.

kpis.name: Institutional giving share
kpis.definition: Share of money raised that came from organisations (companies, foundations, trusts, CSR) rather than individuals.
kpis.formula: Raised from organisations ÷ raised from donors with a type

kpis.name: Amount requested
kpis.definition: Value of funding asked for in the applications in the period.
kpis.formula: Σ amount requested

kpis.name: Share of awards paid
kpis.definition: How much of the amount awarded has been paid out so far.
kpis.formula: Σ amount paid ÷ Σ amount awarded, on awarded grants
pitfalls: Multi-year grants are paid in instalments, so recent awards always look under-paid.

kpis.name: Days to decision
kpis.definition: Average days from application to award decision.
kpis.formula: Average of (award date − application date), one value per grant

variants.label: Award − application date, per row
variants.caveat: No grant ID, so each row is treated as one grant.

kpis.name: Average grant length (months)
kpis.definition: Average planned length of a grant, in months.
kpis.formula: Average of the duration in months (or of end − start date ÷ 30.4 days)

variants.label: End − start date ÷ 30.4375
variants.caveat: From the planned start and end dates, in months of 30.4 days.

kpis.name: Funders
kpis.definition: Distinct funders making grants in the period.
kpis.formula: Count of distinct funders

kpis.name: Median grant
kpis.definition: The middle grant size: half of awards were smaller and half larger.
kpis.formula: Median amount awarded, grants above zero

kpis.name: Average shift length (hours)
kpis.definition: Average hours per volunteer shift worked.
kpis.formula: Volunteer hours ÷ shifts worked

kpis.name: Gifts thanked
kpis.definition: Share of gifts whose donor has been thanked or sent an acknowledgement.
kpis.formula: Gifts acknowledged ÷ gifts with an acknowledgement status (those marked not to be thanked excluded)
pitfalls: Prompt thanks matter more than the share alone: many fundraisers aim to thank within two days of the gift.

kpis.name: Largest gift
kpis.definition: The largest single donation received in the period.
kpis.formula: Maximum donation amount, gifts received

variants.label: Largest amount
variants.caveat: No status column, so a failed or pledged gift can be the largest.

kpis.name: Failed donation rate
kpis.definition: Share of attempted donations that were declined, failed or cancelled.
kpis.formula: Declined, failed or cancelled gifts ÷ gifts with a status

variants.label: Failed rows ÷ rows with a status

pitfalls: Recurring card gifts fail when cards expire; a rising rate often means card details need updating rather than donors leaving.

kpis.name: Pledged and pending amount
kpis.definition: Value of gifts pledged or still being processed, not yet received.
kpis.formula: Σ donation amount with a pending or pledged status

variants.label: Sum of amount, pending or pledged

charts.title: Money raised over time
charts.reason: Money raised per period is an additive total, so columns from a zero baseline compare periods honestly.

charts.title: Donors over time
charts.reason: A distinct count recomputed per period (a donor giving twice counts once), drawn as a line and never summed.

charts.title: Average gift over time
charts.reason: An average recomputed from each period's own gifts, so it reads as a line.

charts.title: New donors over time
charts.reason: Donors acquired per period are discrete counts, so columns from zero compare them.

charts.title: Money raised by campaign
charts.reason: One total compared across named appeals: sorted horizontal bars keep long campaign names readable. Top 10 plus Others.

charts.title: Money raised by channel
charts.reason: The channel mix is a part-to-whole split across a handful of sources, which a donut of at most six slices shows at a glance.

charts.title: Money raised by fund or programme
charts.reason: Where gifts are designated: a part-to-whole split across many funds, which a treemap shows with comparable areas.

charts.title: Money raised by donor type
charts.reason: Individuals against organisations is a part-to-whole split across a few types, shown at a glance as a donut.

charts.title: Gifts by size
charts.reason: Gift sizes are heavily skewed: a histogram of gifts per band shows the many small gifts and the few major ones that the average blurs.

charts.title: Giving concentration by donor (Pareto)
charts.reason: A small share of donors usually gives most of the money: columns per donor with the cumulative share on the same 0–100% axis show how much rests on major donors.

charts.title: Giving by month of the year
charts.reason: Giving is seasonal (year-end, tax-year end, festivals): totals by calendar month, across years, show when appeals land best.

charts.title: Average gift by channel
charts.reason: An average compared across channels: sorted bars of the recomputed average gift, with channels under 30 gifts hidden.

charts.title: Cost to raise a dollar by campaign
charts.reason: Which appeals are efficient: the recomputed cost per unit raised per campaign, sorted.

charts.title: Goal attainment by campaign
charts.reason: How far each appeal got towards its goal, as sorted bars of the recomputed share.

charts.title: Campaign scorecard
charts.reason: Several measures per campaign side by side: a sortable table carries more than any single chart.

charts.title: Donors by year of first gift
charts.reason: Each year's newly acquired donors still on the list, as columns from zero: a quick view of acquisition cohorts.

charts.title: Donors by status
charts.reason: Active, lapsed and new donors as a part-to-whole split across a few statuses.

charts.title: Lifetime giving by donor type
charts.reason: Lifetime totals compared across donor types in sorted bars.

charts.title: Donors by location
charts.reason: Where donors live: sorted bars, top 12 plus Others.

charts.title: Donors by lifetime giving
charts.reason: Lifetime giving is skewed towards a few major donors: a histogram of donors per band shows the spread the average hides.

charts.title: Donors by number of gifts
charts.reason: How many donors gave once and how many keep giving: donors per band of gift count.

charts.title: Amount awarded over time
charts.reason: Awards per period are additive totals, so columns from a zero baseline compare them honestly.

charts.title: Grants awarded over time
charts.reason: The number of awards per period, as a line beside the amounts.

charts.title: Amount awarded by programme
charts.reason: One total compared across programmes in sorted bars, drilling into the grantees.

charts.title: Amount awarded by location
charts.reason: Where the money goes: sorted bars per beneficiary location, top 12 plus Others.

charts.title: Amount awarded by funder
charts.reason: The funder mix as a part-to-whole split across a handful of funders.

charts.title: Grants by size
charts.reason: Grant sizes are skewed: a histogram of grants per band shows the many small awards and the few large ones.

charts.title: Funding concentration by grantee (Pareto)
charts.reason: How much of the funding goes to a few organisations: columns per grantee with the cumulative share on the same 0–100% axis.

charts.title: Application success rate by programme
charts.reason: A rate compared across programmes: sorted bars of the recomputed success rate, with programmes under 20 applications hidden.

charts.title: Programme scorecard
charts.reason: Several measures per programme side by side: a sortable table carries more than any single chart.

charts.title: Volunteer hours over time
charts.reason: Hours per period are additive totals, so columns from a zero baseline compare them honestly.

charts.title: Active volunteers over time
charts.reason: A distinct count recomputed per period, drawn as a line and never summed.

charts.title: Volunteer hours by role
charts.reason: One total compared across roles and activities in sorted bars, top 10 plus Others.

charts.title: Volunteer hours by programme
charts.reason: Where volunteer time goes, as a part-to-whole split across programmes.

charts.title: Hours concentration by volunteer (Pareto)
charts.reason: A core of volunteers usually gives most of the hours: columns per volunteer with the cumulative share on the same 0–100% axis show how much rests on them.

charts.title: When volunteers serve
charts.reason: Two time dimensions and one count: a weekday × hour heatmap shows when shifts are filled, for rota planning.

charts.title: No-show rate by role
charts.reason: A rate compared across roles: sorted bars of the recomputed no-show rate, with roles under 20 shifts hidden.

charts.title: Volunteer scorecard
charts.reason: Several measures per volunteer side by side: a sortable table carries more than any single chart.

pitfalls: Pledges are promises, not money: keep them apart from gifts received, and watch for a pledge and its payments both appearing in one file.
Soft credits, split designations and matching gifts can list one gift on several rows; count gifts and donors with DISTINCT IDs and add amounts from the hard-credit rows only.
A few major gifts dominate most totals; read the median gift and the donor Pareto beside the average.
Giving is seasonal (year-end, tax-year end, Giving Tuesday, festivals): compare a month with the same month a year earlier, not with the month before.
Donors whose first gift predates the file look new, and donor retention needs at least two full years of history.
Grant awards are commitments, often paid over several years: never add awards and payments together.
